ABSTRACT Background Accumulation of body fat and dyslipidemia are associated with the development of obesity and cardiometabolic diseases. Moreover, the degree to which lipids can be metabolized has been cited as a determinant of cardiometabolic health and prolonged endurance capacity. In the backdrop of increasing obesity and cardiometabolic diseases, lipid metabolism and its modulation by physical activity, dietary adjustments, and supplementation play a significant role in maintaining health and endurance. Food-derived oligopeptides, such as rice and soybean peptides, have been shown to directly regulate abnormal lipid metabolism or promote hypolipidemia and fat oxidation in cell culture models, animal models, and human studies. However, whether supplementation with oligopeptides derived from multiple food sources can promote lipid degradation and fat oxidation in athletes remains unclear. Therefore, in a randomized controlled crossover trial, we investigated the impact of food-derived oligopeptide supplementation before and during exercise on lipid metabolism in young male cyclists. Methods Sixteen young male cyclists (age: 17.0 ± 1.0 years; height: 178.4 ± 6.9 cm; body mass: 68.7 ± 12.7 kg, body mass index: 21.5 ± 3.4 kg/m 2 ; maximum oxygen uptake: 56.3 ± 5.8 mL/min/kg) participated in this randomized controlled crossover trial. Each participant drank two beverages, one containing a blend of three food-derived oligopeptides (treatment, 0.5 g/kg body weight in total) and the other without (control), with a 2-week washout period between two experiments. The cyclists completed a one-day pattern protocol that consisted of intraday fasting, 30 min of sitting still, 85 min of prolonged exercise plus a 5-min sprint (PE), a short recovery period of 60 min, a 20-min time trial (TT), and recovery till next morning. Blood samples were collected for biochemical analyses of serum lipids and other biomarkers. We analyzed plasma triglyceride species (TGs), free amino acids (FAAs), and tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle intermediates using omics methods. In addition, exhaled gas was collected to assess the fat oxidation rate. Results Five of 20 plasma FAAs were elevated pre-exercise (pre-Ex) only 20 min after oligopeptide ingestion, and most FAAs were markedly increased post PE and TT. Serum levels of TG and non-esterified fatty acids were lower in the experimental condition than in the control condition at the post PE and TT assessments, respectively. Further, the omics analysis of plasma TGs for the experimental condition demonstrated that most TGs were lower post PE and at the next fasting when compared with control levels. Simultaneously, the fat oxidation rate began to increase only 20 min after ingestion and during the preceding 85 min of PE. Levels of TCA cycle intermediates did not differ between the conditions. Conclusions The study noted that continuous ingestion of food-derived oligopeptides accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid uptake, and fat oxidation during both sedentary and exercise states. Elevated circulating and intracellular FAA flux may modulate the selection of substrates for metabolic pathways in conjunction with the release of neuroendocrinological factors that slow down carbohydrate metabolism via acetyl coenzyme A feedback inhibition. This may increase the availability of fatty acids for energy production, with FAAs supplying more substrates for the TCA cycle. The findings of this study provide novel insight into strategies for promoting lipid metabolism in populations with dyslipidemia-related metabolic disorders such as obesity and for improving physiological functioning during endurance training. However, the absence of a non-exercising control group and verification of long-term supplementation effects was a limitation. Future studies will emphasize the impacts of whole protein supplementation as a control and of combined food-derived peptides or oligopeptides with probiotics and healthy food components on lipid metabolism in individuals who exercise. Introduction Excess accumulation of body fat is associated with obesity, dyslipidemia, and cardiometabolic diseases including, hypertension, stroke, type 2 diabetes, and several types of cancer [ 1 ]. In general, strategies for improving lipolysis/fat oxidation include increased participation in physical activities, adjustments to dietary patterns, and supplementation [ 2 ]. Physical activity improves lipid metabolism by enhancing lipolysis and fat oxidation. Researchers have observed a higher fat oxidation rate in athletes than in untrained or non-elite participants during high-intensity exercise [ 3 , 4 ]. Endogenous triacylglycerol is an important source of fuel for endurance exercise, and its oxidation progressively increases during exercise [ 5 , 6 ]. In competitive long-distance runners, an increased ratio of fat utilization can partly spare glycogen for the later sprint and improve exercise performance. Healthy dietary patterns and nutritional supplements are also beneficial for improving fat intake and lipid metabolism. Protein or amino acid supplementation is prevalent in sports nutrition. Evidence shows that high-protein diets or dietary supplements, particularly amino acid mixtures containing branched chain amino acids (BCAAs), can reduce body fat and improve dyslipidemia when combined with physical activity by stimulating lipolysis and maximizing fat oxidation [ 7–11 ]. Furthermore, elevated circulating BCAA levels in individuals with low physical activity are linked to a high body fat percentage, low fat oxidation, and impaired metabolism [ 12 ]. At the same time, BCAA deprivation impairs lipid oxidation in C2C12 myotubes [ 13 ]. Moreover, leucine/valine metabolites such as β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate and β-aminoisobutyric acid improve fat oxidation and increase energy expenditure [ 14 , 15 ] in adipose tissue and skeletal muscles. Individual amino acids such as arginine (Arg), tyrosine (Tyr), and tryptophan (Trp) modulate circulating levels of neurotransmitters or hormones such as growth hormones and catecholamines, which may regulate glucose and lipid metabolism during exercise [ 16 ]. Food-derived peptides are increasingly used in ordinary food products, sports nutrition products, nutraceuticals, specific medical supplements, and therapeutic food products [ 17–21 ]. Food-derived oligopeptides formed by condensing 2–10 amino acids can be absorbed as free amino acids (FAAs) or partial oligopeptides [ 22 ]. Food-derived oligopeptides such as rice and soybean peptides directly regulate abnormal lipid metabolism or promote hypolipidemia and fat oxidation in cell culture models, animal models, and human studies [ 23–26 ]. The effect of supplementation with multi-food-derived oligopeptides on lipid degradation and fat oxidation in athletes/fitness enthusiasts has not been explored. We hypothesized that this would improve lipid metabolism under various physiological states in relatively static conditions during moderate–intensity exercise. Therefore, in this study, we examined the effects of ingesting beverages with and without a blend of three food-derived oligopeptides, which have been shown to have the beneficial effects of alleviating exercise-induced fatigue and skeletal muscle damage [ 27 , 28 ] and improving immunity and metabolism [ 29 , 30 ], on lipid degradation and fat oxidation under various physiological conditions. These included sitting still (SS), prolonged exercise (PE), a time trial (TT) after a short rest period, and recovery till the next morning in young cyclists. Our findings will help endurance athletes, fitness enthusiasts, and populations with metabolic disorders in choosing dietary supplements. Our findings will also be essential and referentially significant to future studies, along with the increasing development and broad utilization of food-derived oligopeptides as popular dietary supplements, especially combined with probiotics and other nutritional components in various physical activities.

extracted_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled crossover trial investigated the impact of continuous multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS) on intraday lipid metabolism in young male cyclists. The study found that FOPS accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) uptake, and fat oxidation during both sedentary and exercise states. It also increased plasma free amino acids (FAAs) and post-exercise blood glucose, suggesting a modulation of metabolic substrate selection for improved endurance performance and cardiometabolic health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous ingestion of multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants ingested a blend of three food-derived oligopeptides (from soybean, wheat, and fish skin collagen proteins) and 6% carbohydrate with electrolytes. The total dosage was 0.5 g/kg body weight, administered in multiple servings (0.05 g/kg body weight each) throughout a one-day exercise protocol. Specifically, approximately 7g of oligopeptides were ingested 20 minutes pre-exercise, followed by continuous ingestion totaling approximately 31.5g to 35g during the 24-hour trial. The protocol included intraday fasting, 30 minutes of sitting still, 85 minutes of prolonged exercise plus a 5-minute sprint, a 60-minute recovery, and a 20-minute time trial. No dose-response comparisons for varying oligopeptide amounts were reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma and Serum (also implied in Adipose tissues, Liver)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Lipid Concentration and Metabolic Breakdown Rate

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: FOPS significantly lowered serum/plasma TG levels post-prolonged exercise and time trial, and at subsequent fasting, compared to control. Most TGs were decreased (e.g., 45% of 101 TGs in the FOPS group vs. 3% in control at 'no FOPS' fasting condition). Average percentage changes post-TT and at fasting were -22% and -10% respectively, with FOPS. Mildly lower serum TG levels were observed within 20 minutes of initial oligopeptide ingestion. The treatment promoted whole-body TG breakdown, including rapid breakdown in adipose tissues and liver.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Primary form of energy storage, transport of lipids, and structural components of cell membranes; mobilization of stored fat for energy production.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Continuous FOPS supplementation before, during, and after prolonged exercise (PE) and time trial (TT) sessions, and during fasting and sedentary states.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown and enhanced fat utilization contribute to improved lipid metabolism, sustained energy supply, and potentially enhanced endurance capacity, recovery, and cardiometabolic health by preventing fat accumulation.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Lipid Concentration and Cellular Uptake Rate

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Serum NEFA levels were lower in the FOPS group compared to control post-prolonged exercise (PE) and time trial (TT). Greater increases in NEFA (p = 0.046) were observed when FOPS was not provided ('no FOPS' condition). FOPS promoted whole-body NEFA uptake and muscle FFA uptake, which did not occur in the control condition.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Primary source of energy, key signaling molecules in metabolic regulation; transport form of fatty acids readily available for energy production; involved in fatty acid transport into cells for oxidation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: FOPS supplementation before, during, and after prolonged exercise and time trial, including sedentary and fasting states.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased NEFA uptake and altered fat mobilization/utilization, promoting fat oxidation, which is beneficial for endurance performance by sparing glycogen reserves, providing sustained energy, and improving cardiometabolic health.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Free Amino Acids (FAAs), including Glucogenic (GAAs), Essential (EAAs), Branched-Chain (BCAAs), Ketogenic (KAAs/GKAAs), Aromatic (AAAs), and specific amino acids (e.g., Arg, Tyr, Orn, Gln, Glu, Lys, Asp, Ala, Met)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: FOPS led to significantly higher plasma FAA levels. Five of 20 plasma FAAs (GAAs) were elevated within 20 minutes post-ingestion (pre-exercise). Most FAAs (including 17 of 20 species covering EAAs, BCAAs, KAAs/GKAAs, AAAs) were markedly increased post-prolonged exercise (PE) and remained higher than control post-time trial (TT), despite some reduction from post-PE levels. Elevated circulating Arg, Tyr, and Orn were noted. In the control group, EAAs, BCAAs, and KAAs/GKAAs gradually decreased over time, significantly lower post-TT compared to pre-exercise. Seven specific FAAs (Arg, Gln, Glu, Lys, Asp, Ala, Met) were consumed more during recovery and TT periods regardless of group post-TT.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Building blocks for proteins, energy substrates, and precursors for various metabolic pathways; they modulate substrate selection and can influence neuroendocrinological factors.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: FOPS supplementation before, during (prolonged exercise, time trial), and after exercise, and during sedentary states.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased FAA flux indicates enhanced amino acid availability, supporting energy metabolism, muscle repair, and recovery. This may modulate metabolic pathways by slowing carbohydrate breakdown, increasing fatty acid availability for energy, supplying substrates for the TCA cycle, and supporting muscle glycogen resynthesis, benefiting endurance, metabolic health, and training adaptations.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Whole-body (calculated from exhaled gas/RER) and Muscle

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The fat oxidation rate was significantly higher in the FOPS group, starting within 10-20 minutes after initial ingestion and continuing during steady-state (SS) and the initial 85 minutes of prolonged exercise (PE). The average RER was lower in the FOPS group during SS and the first 85 minutes of PE, indicating greater fat utilization. While slightly lower during the latter 5 minutes of PE and the 20-minute time trial, overall, FOPS promoted whole-body and muscle fat oxidation during rest and prolonged exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: The metabolic process of generating energy (ATP) from fatty acids; the rate at which the body uses fat as an energy substrate.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: FOPS supplementation at rest, during steady-state exercise, and throughout prolonged exercise and time trial periods.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved lipid metabolism and an enhanced capacity to utilize fat for energy, which is crucial for endurance performance by sparing glycogen stores and improving metabolic efficiency. This is beneficial for athletes and populations with dyslipidemia, enhancing training adaptations and overall health.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle intermediates (pyruvate, fumarate, succinate, malate,  -ketoglutaric acid, citrate) and lactate

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels of these intermediates increased post-prolonged exercise (PE) and remained elevated post-time trial (TT), indicating active aerobic respiration. However, no significant differences were observed between the FOPS and control groups at any time point.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Key components of the central metabolic pathway for aerobic energy production (cellular respiration); lactate is a product of anaerobic glycolysis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During and after prolonged exercise and time trial periods, with and without FOPS supplementation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased levels suggest enhanced metabolic flux through the TCA cycle due to exercise. The lack of differential effect with FOPS implies that oligopeptide supplementation did not directly alter the overall concentration or flux of these specific intermediates, suggesting its influence on lipid metabolism might occur upstream or via alternative compensatory mechanisms.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Blood urea levels were higher post-prolonged exercise (PE) compared to pre-exercise. In the control group, BU levels increased over time. In the FOPS group, increased BU was associated with arginine metabolism/biosynthesis.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An end-product of protein catabolism, primarily from amino acid deamination, reflecting altered amino acid or energy metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-prolonged exercise, and over time during prolonged exercise in both FOPS and control conditions.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: In the control group, it suggests muscle proteolysis to supply FAAs for energy. In the FOPS group, it indicates increased amino acid metabolism, potentially for energy production or other metabolic pathways influenced by FOPS.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: LDL-C levels were higher in the FOPS group compared to control in the 'no FOPS' condition (p = 0.051). A significant decrease in LDL-C was observed in the control group at 'no FOPS' but not in the FOPS group. There was also a significantly increased synthesis of LDL-C observed the morning after the test session in the FOPS group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol to cells for various physiological processes; high levels are associated with increased cardiovascular risk.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Comparing FOPS and control groups under 'no FOPS' conditions and in the morning after the FOPS supplementation and exercise protocol.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates alterations in cholesterol transport and metabolism, suggesting a distinct metabolic response in the FOPS group potentially influenced by exercise and supplementation. Sustained increases could be associated with cardiovascular risk.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A greater decrease in TCH levels was observed in the control group at 'no FOPS' condition, but not in the FOPS group. There was also a significantly increased synthesis of TCH observed the morning after the test session in the FOPS group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An essential structural component of cell membranes and a precursor for steroid hormones and bile acids.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Comparing FOPS and control groups under 'no FOPS' conditions and in the morning after the FOPS supplementation and exercise protocol.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered overall cholesterol metabolism, with a less pronounced decrease in the FOPS group during the 'no FOPS' condition and increased synthesis post-exercise, suggesting a distinct and complex metabolic response to FOPS and exercise. Sustained increases could be associated with cardiovascular risk.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Greater increases in  -HBA (p = 0.007) were observed in the 'no FOPS' condition compared to the 'FOPS' condition within the treatment group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A ketone body serving as an alternative energy source derived from fat metabolism, particularly during low carbohydrate availability or prolonged exercise.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Comparing conditions with and without FOPS within the treatment group, particularly during exercise and recovery.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased fat oxidation and ketone body production for energy, suggesting a compensatory shift in fuel utilization under metabolic stress when FOPS is absent.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences were observed in HDL-C levels between the FOPS and control groups at any time point.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol from peripheral tissues back to the liver, often referred to as 'good' cholesterol.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Throughout the study, comparing FOPS and control groups during exercise and recovery.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: No differential impact of FOPS or exercise conditions was noted on this marker of cardiovascular health, suggesting its stability under these specific experimental parameters.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The average blood glucose level post-time trial (TT) was significantly higher in the FOPS group compared to the control group (p = 0.041), maintaining a higher level during the high-intensity TT period.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for cells, crucial for maintaining energy homeostasis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-time trial, and after recovery during a high-intensity time trial period, following FOPS supplementation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher post-exercise blood glucose in the FOPS group suggests better maintenance of glucose homeostasis or altered glucose metabolism, contributing to sustained energy supply during intense exercise, preventing hypoglycemia, and potentially supporting performance.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Serum hormones (unspecified, but including glucagon, with implied potential influence on growth hormones, epinephrine, norepinephrine, dopamine)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Several hormone levels fluctuated with exercise, but no statistically significant differences were observed between the FOPS and control groups at any time point. Specifically, circulating glucagon levels did not change with FOPS.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulate various physiological processes, including metabolism, stress response, and fluid balance, with glucagon specifically raising blood glucose.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Throughout exercise and recovery periods, with FOPS supplementation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: The lack of differential impact on overall hormone regulation suggests that FOPS primarily influences metabolic substrates directly rather than acutely altering major hormonal signaling, implying alternative mechanisms for metabolic modulation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Following FOPS ingestion, liver glycogen breakdown was inhibited, and its resynthesis was promoted.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Storage form of glucose in the liver, crucial for maintaining blood glucose homeostasis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Following FOPS ingestion during exercise and recovery periods.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved energy substrate availability, which helps maintain blood glucose levels, spare glycogen during exercise, and replenish stores during recovery, beneficial for endurance performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: FOPS-induced neuroendocrinological factors were noted to activate HSL and LPL, leading to rapid triglyceride breakdown in adipose tissues and the liver.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Enzymes crucial for the breakdown of triglycerides, with HSL mobilizing stored fat from adipocytes and LPL clearing triglycerides from lipoproteins.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Mediates rapid fat breakdown and mobilization for energy, significantly contributing to improved lipid metabolism and efficient fuel utilization.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated Acetyl CoA levels were observed, resulting from increased cellular ketogenic amino acids (KAAs) and simultaneous fatty acid  -oxidation. This may slow carbohydrate breakdown and increase the availability of fatty acids for the TCA cycle.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Key intermediate in metabolism, linking glycolysis, fatty acid oxidation, and the TCA cycle.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Following FOPS ingestion, particularly during exercise and recovery, linked to KAA conversion and fatty acid  -oxidation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a shift towards increased fatty acid utilization for energy, helping to spare carbohydrate metabolism and optimize energy supply, thereby enhancing exercise adaptations and potentially improving health and sports performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated circulating levels of oligopeptides were implied and speculated to occur following continuous ingestion.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Modulate the release of lipolytic neuroendocrinological factors to promote lipid metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Continuous ingestion of multi-food-derived oligopeptides during the study protocol.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Closely linked to promoting whole-body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid uptake, and fat oxidation, contributing to improved metabolic function.
